title: The Distrusted
subtitle: His distrust of everything is precisely what makes him trustworthy.

items.text: The Distrusted

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Bertolt, age ...

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Shall we skip the formalities and get started, comrade? Let's not waste each other's time.
The officer interrupts with soldier-like efficiency.
The interrogator's face sours. He does not enjoy the disruption of his tiny sense of authority.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: How's our soldier faring in captivity? Can you give me a glimpse of the outcome, comrade?

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Private Aleksei is calm, coherent, and cooperating with the interrogation. My role is only to interrogate, the verdict is up to the judiciary.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: But the judge is going to need you to provide the evidence.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Yes, but the outcome is more up to you and your subordinates. My submission will be shaped by your narrative.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Fine. Rest assured, you will learn what you want to know.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: By the way, how's the girl?

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Miss Lilya is in another room for questioning. Don't worry, we treat our trainees with care, especially since she's so young.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Those who've experienced war and artillery fire can hardly be called "young" anymore.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Personally, I agree with this sentiment, but that's a topic for another day. As you said, let's not waste time.
The interrogator takes out another set of documents.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: The prisoner mentioned that you saved a local civilian after the explosion, which led to an argument. What happened after that?

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: What happened between Private Aleksei and the auxiliary soldier Hassan, both of whom were your subordinates?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Nothing much. Just an ordinary quarrel between comrades, like an everyday quarrel you might have with your wife.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Honestly, you guys out here, assigned so far from the front lines, can sometimes get a little too ... well, you know.
Hearing this, the interrogator loosens his collar, revealing the scars on his neck and chest.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Two years ago, we were pulling out of the mountain pass. My squad was responsible for covering the rear and fending off pursuit.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: After the shooting subsided, only two of us survived in that valley—myself, and the officer I later carried back to base safely.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: That's the end of that story.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: The Military Discipline Department is still waiting for our report. We need to wrap up this case quickly, as the higher-ups expect us to work efficiently.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: The admiral wants us to tighten military discipline, and all the bases currently have problems that our oversight team must solve.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: You should understand that a bunch of armed thugs can't be called an army unless they're firmly bound by discipline and order.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: This is especially important when it comes to those unstable arcanists.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Strictly speaking, interrogations like this should be handled by the Interrogations Department, but for the time being, we are tasked with this duty.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: You've been on the front lines. You should understand Zeno's current predicament better than most. We have lost too many of our comrades in the "Storm."

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Please continue, Lieutenant.
The officer pauses for a moment, then speaks again.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: To retrieve the lost documents hidden in the valley, we ventured deep into the mountains, searching for our target.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Such was the directive from the headquarters.
In the Mountains, Juhalerat

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: A month ago, we received an order to clear both sides of the road in the mountains—to leave not a single tree standing. But no one bothered to do it.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: So when we left the wilderness and followed a trail deeper into the forest, everyone was on high alert.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We spoke little. The chirping of birds filled the silence, taking me back to those long summer days in Odessa.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Lilya's device guided us, but in that place, knowing the direction and finding an actual path were two different things.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: My hometown doesn't have nearly as many trees as this, my little comrade.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: I'm from Rayashki. You know the place? A cold, faraway little town that has a partnership with Zeno.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Maybe it was because to this connection that I was chosen as a new recruit for advanced training at the Zeno Arms Academy.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You never told me, Comrade Aleksei.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: I thought you knew, sir. Didn't all of our files pass through your hands?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You didn't know?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I don't pay much mind to these things, but Rayashki is a nice place. I've been there before.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: You've actually been there?!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Indeed. The people there are united, brave, and kind, forging a homeland that is both strong and splendid.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: That's wonderful! Truth be told, it's been years since I've been home.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: In two months you will be able to take your leave and return home. Rayashki is thriving now, and I'm sure your mother has been eagerly waiting for your arrival.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: She's always worried about me, sending letters and money ... but I don't need the money. Her letters are more important.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Hah, my father thinks she's a overreacting. Having a son on the front lines is an honor, a mother shouldn't worry so much.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: All the men in our family have served. My father was also in Zeno's forces, but he retired a few years ago after returning from Prague.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: And my grandfather was a war hero. He earned his medals in Bialystok.
When talking about home and family, Aleksei's face lights up with a bright smile.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Your whole family is incredible, Aleksei.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Yes, and we have never compromised our principles—from my grandfather, to my father, to me, and hopefully to ... to my future son.
He blushes at this point, looking a bit timid.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Zeno is truly grateful for you and your father's service, Aleksei.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Service? No, Commander. We call it allegiance! Our loyalty is eternal!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Aleksei is a young man of unshakable convictions, untainted by the various vices of the barracks.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: He is committed to changing the locals' hostility toward us, because in order for Zeno to maintain a long-term presence there, fostering good relations with the locals is essential.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: In the grand scheme of things, his approach is correct.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Family, country, and military—he is loyal to these "old-fashioned" ideals, and that is precisely what we need.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: In these turbulent times, comrade, a brave and loyal heart shines brighter than a thousand suns.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: But he is simply too young, too ... impetuous and naive.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Boss ...

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We remained vigilant. The fearless Hassan was leading the way with comrades from the region.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: They seemed to know every hill and tree in the area.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Recruiting local auxiliaries was a wise move. These amiable local allies have done much for Zeno and deserve proper recognition.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: There's only one path forward. We'd better be careful.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Want me to take a look from the sky?

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Don't, comrade. If you fly up there and a gun is pointed at you down here, you'll be an easy target.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: My people have hunted eagles in these mountains here, for thousands of years ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Tsk. The Red-38 is no bird. Are you giving your people too much credit, or are you doubting my ability to fly?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Hassan's right, don't expose yourself unnecessarily. Stay behind the group near Aleksei, and cover our rear.
Lilya grumbles, but obeys the order and returns to the back of the group.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Doesn't it seem a bit too quiet, boss?
The wind roars into the distance, sweeping through the entire valley.
Hassan kicks a pebble off a cliff, watching it land in a riverbed below the mountains.
In the distance, a majestic mountain peak shines in all its glory, its snowy top sparkling under the blazing Juhalerat sun.
The mighty Hindu Kush, where even eagles dare not fly.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: I'd prefer it if I had a few locals to chat with. Slow down, boss, I'll take a few men ahead, you follow.
Hassan gestures and calls out in the local tongue. The few locals from the auxiliary forces follow him.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: They were adept at mountain warfare, but they clung to their own firearms, unaccustomed to Zeno's arcanum weaponry.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: These comrades from Juhalerat were more resilient than other soldiers, and they knew the importance of obedience. Hassan seemed well respected by them.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Why do they get to go to the front? I can do that too.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Because they know the terrain, and you don't.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Just follow your orders, Aleksei.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Are we headed in the right direction, little falcon chick? Take out your arcanum trinket and give it a look.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: About two kilometers to go.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: In a straight line?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Right.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: It'll take about two hours on foot. There's nothing but mountains here, and if not mountains, then trees, and if not trees, then rocks.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And if not rocks, then people.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Our people, their people.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Comrade Lilya pointed the way as Hassan cleared the path ahead. We made our way over the hill and continued on a dirt road between the mountains.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: After a narrow pass flanked by rock walls, the mountain trail became more winding. But ahead, we were greeted by houses and watchtowers.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: It was then, gunfire erupted from both the front and rear of our formation.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: D**n! All hands, battle positions!
